root_cause: divide() has no guard for None inputs, causing an unhandled TypeError at runtime.
explanation: The function divide(a, b) performs the division a / b without first checking whether a or b is None. When either argument is None, Python raises a TypeError ('unsupported operand type(s) for /: NoneType and int') instead of the expected ValueError. Adding an explicit None-check before the division and raising ValueError corrects the behaviour.
